news.headline: NeurAxis Expands Payer Coverage with New Policies
news.summary: NeurAxis announced additional medical policy coverage decisions for its IB-Stim PENFS technology, adding regional health plan coverage worth over 500,000 covered lives in the Mid-Atlantic region. CEO Brian Carrico said the new coverage broadens patient access and strengthens the company's reimbursement network as it builds on the new Category I CPT code for PENFS.

news.headline: NeurAxis to Host Second Quarter 2026 Results and Business Update Call on Tuesday, August 11, 2026
news.summary: NeurAxis confirmed it will report summarized second-quarter 2026 financial results (period ended June 30, 2026) before market open on August 11, 2026, followed by a 9:00 am ET conference call to discuss results and provide a business update. Sell-side estimates reportedly model roughly $2.0M in Q2 revenue and a per-share loss near $0.32.

news.headline: Neuraxis Files Form S-3 Registering Shares for Resale by Selling Stockholders
news.summary: NeurAxis filed a new shelf registration statement covering roughly 1.92 million shares of common stock for resale by selling stockholders, including shares previously issued to shareholders and directors for services plus shares underlying restricted stock units. The filing does not raise new capital for the company but creates a potential secondary-sale overhang as previously issued shares become freely tradable.

news.headline: Neuraxis Declares Q2 Stock Dividend on Series B Preferred
news.summary: NeurAxis's board declared its second-quarter 2026 dividend on Series B Preferred Stock payable entirely in shares of common stock (approximately 80,463 new shares) rather than cash, based on accrued dividends divided by $2.38 per share. The dividend was paid July 29, 2026 to holders of record as of July 21, 2026, conserving company cash while modestly diluting common shareholders.

catalysts.label: Q2 2026 earnings release and conference call
catalysts.detail: NeurAxis will release summarized second-quarter 2026 financial results (period ended June 30, 2026) before market open and host a conference call at 9:00 am ET; sell-side estimates reportedly model roughly $2.0M in Q2 revenue and an EPS loss near $0.32.

catalysts.label: Continued payer coverage expansion for IB-Stim
catalysts.detail: NeurAxis continues to pursue additional commercial and Medicaid payer medical policy coverage decisions state-by-state, most recently adding over 500,000 covered lives in the Mid-Atlantic region on August 4, 2026, building on the Category I CPT code that took effect January 1, 2026.

catalysts.label: Targeted path to cash-flow breakeven
catalysts.detail: Management has previously guided toward reaching cash-flow breakeven during 2026, contingent on continued IB-Stim revenue growth following the new AMA Category I CPT code for PENFS effective January 1, 2026.

catalysts.label: Rectal Expulsion Device (RED) commercial relaunch
catalysts.detail: Commercialization of the adult RED constipation-screening device was paused following a CPT coding change in early 2026; management has indicated it is seeking clarity to resume the RED commercial ramp.

catalysts.label: Q3 2026 earnings release (expected)
catalysts.detail: Based on NeurAxis's quarterly reporting cadence, the next results after the August 11 Q2 call would be the Q3 2026 report, typically released in mid-to-late November.

pulse: NeurAxis is a small-cap medtech commercializing IB-Stim, an FDA-cleared PENFS neuromodulation device for pediatric functional abdominal pain, which is now benefiting from a new AMA Category I CPT code (effective January 1, 2026) and a steady drumbeat of incremental payer coverage wins, most recently over 500,000 additional Mid-Atlantic covered lives announced August 4, 2026. The company is otherwise quiet on the news front over the past six weeks aside from routine items (a July 9 Series B stock dividend and a July 23 resale shelf registration), with all eyes now on the August 11, 2026 Q2 earnings call to see whether the 80% revenue-growth pace from Q1 and the path toward 2026 cash-flow breakeven are holding up. The stock remains volatile and still carries dilution risk via its at-the-market program and newly registered resale shares, even as analysts (Craig-Hallum) hold Strong Buy ratings with price targets around $11-13.
